question: Rani and Adya, working separately, can finish a task in 12 days and 16 days, respectively. They work in stretches of one day alternately. If Rani starts working first, then the task will be completed in
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(12, 16) = 48 units.

Efficiencies: Rani = 48 ÷ 12 = 4 units/day, Adya = 48 ÷ 16 = 3 units/day.

Work done in 2 days (Rani + Adya) = 4 + 3 = 7 units.

Work in 12 days (6 cycles) = 6 × 7 = 42 units. Remaining work = 48 − 42 = 6 units.

Day 13: Rani does 4 units. Remaining = 2 units. Day 14: Adya takes 2/3 day to finish.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 ²/₃ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Rani = 12 days

Time taken by Adya = 16 days

They work in stretches of one day alternately, starting with Rani.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Rani
 12
 48
 4
 
 

 Adya
 16
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done in 1st day by Rani = 4 units

⇒ Work done in 2nd day by Adya = 3 units

⇒ Work done in a 2-day cycle = 4 + 3 = 7 units

⇒ Number of complete 2-day cycles in 48 units = 48 ÷ 7 = 6 cycles

⇒ Work done in 12 days (6 cycles) = 6 × 7 = 42 units

⇒ Remaining work = 48 − 42 = 6 units

⇒ On the 13th day, Rani does 4 units of work.

⇒ Work done in 13 days = 42 + 4 = 46 units

⇒ Remaining work = 48 − 46 = 2 units

⇒ On the 14th day, Adya completes the remaining work.

⇒ Time taken by Adya = Remaining work ÷ Efficiency = 2/3 day

⇒ Total time taken = 13 days + 2/3 day = 13 ²/₃ days

**∴ The correct answer is 13 ²/₃ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Days Work

When individuals work on alternate days, find the total work done in one complete cycle (usually 2 days) and use it to find the maximum possible full cycles before calculating the leftover work.

Work and Efficiency Ratio

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the time taken ratio is A : B, then the efficiency ratio is B : A.

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to Time and Work, an inlet pipe has a positive efficiency (filling) while an outlet pipe has a negative efficiency (emptying).
